change.title: pr-38446-flat
change.description: Implement recovery key support for user storage providers
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Stale local recovery codes remain when codes are stored in user storage
findings.body: When updateCredential returns true, the local DB provider's createCredential is skipped. The provider's createCredential is what replaces an existing local recovery-codes credential. A user who already has local codes and whose storage later accepts them keeps a stale local credential. RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential prefers the federated one, so login works, but the old local codes are never deleted. Is this intended?

findings.title: Provider looked up eagerly and unrelated reindent of an existing method
findings.body: The CredentialProvider is fetched before it is known to be needed, so it is unused when user storage handles the credential. The provider ID is also a hard-coded string, where the removed code used RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID. Lines 76-84 are a whitespace-only reindent of getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory that has nothing to do with this change.

findings.title: Test storage never marks recovery codes as used and returns a credential with no id
findings.body: getCredentials builds the model with createFromValues, which sets no id. It also treats every code as unused, and isValid (line 340) never consumes a code. The test therefore only exercises the first-code path. It does not cover the all-codes-used branch in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator, where removeStoredCredentialById is called with a null id for a federated credential. Tests for that branch would show whether it behaves correctly.

findings.title: Typo in config alias and unused delay parameter
findings.body: The alias "delayed-suthenticator-config" is misspelled. The delay argument is always 0, and the delayed-authenticator it configures adds nothing to this test. The test also mixes org.junit.Assert with the wildfly assertTrue import.

contracts.action: Recovery codes are created via CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential (user storage first, local DB fallback)
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous code called the local recovery-codes CredentialProvider.createCredential directly. The OTP setup path already tries user storage first.
contracts.before_after: Before, codes always went to the local DB. Now updateCredential on the credential manager is tried first. If it returns false, the local provider is used as before.
contracts.visible_effect: For federated users whose storage supports the type, the codes live in storage. Other users are unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: Not verified: whether a stale local credential is left behind when storage accepts the codes (see finding on CredentialHelper).

contracts.action: Recovery credential lookup now checks federated credentials, then local ones, in the login form authenticator and in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous code used getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream only.
contracts.before_after: The federated stream is now consulted first, and the local stream only if nothing federated matches.
contracts.visible_effect: The login form can show the next code to enter for storage-backed credentials.
contracts.failure_mode: The all-codes-used removal calls removeStoredCredentialById, which affects only local credentials, so a federated credential is not removed.

summary: The change lets recovery codes be stored in and read from user storage. I found no blocking defects. The notes are minor: a possible stale local credential when storage accepts the codes, unrelated reindentation in CredentialHelper, and thin test-storage coverage. The test also has a misspelled alias and an unused delay parameter. I only read the code and did not run or build anything.
